exposure: Maternal obesity (using international and South Asian specific BMI cut-offs)
cohort: 8478 pregnant women (South Asian and White British) participating in the Born in Bradford (BiB) cohort study
finding: While applying South Asian BMI cut-offs increased the prevalence of obesity in Pakistani women, BMI as a continuous variable was a better predictor of adverse pregnancy outcomes than any specific BMI cut-off point.
mod_finding: There was a positive linear relationship between maternal BMI and prevalence of adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes, including mode of birth.
